raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Apply canonical Miles updates directly to live SGLang weights, and load HF-base delta publications on fresh or restarted engines. Paired [Miles #3894](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3894); [tracker #3734](https://github.com/radixark/miles/issues/3734).

## Modifications

- **Lifecycle/API:** four Miles-facing routes: `/get_gpu_delta_info`, `/update_weights_from_gpu_delta`, `/get_gpu_delta_status` and `/clear_gpu_delta_state`. One update carries the negotiated participants, session ID and publication descriptor. Tokenizer initialization and worker-count admission run once at the public request boundary. SGLang prepares while serving, then owns pause/fence/apply, all-rank acknowledgement and resume. APPLIED IPC carries identity/provenance/state/pause boundaries and the applied/target-version verdict; full metrics remain in RESUMED and status. Internal preparation failure is released; an uncertain XOR after apply dispatch is never replayed.
- **Recovery/deployment:** rolling and fresh-engine HF-base updates share the explicit descriptor contract; there is no manifest-only loader. Resources remain cached by default (`release_state=False`). `release_state=True` performs the existing all-rank close/shared-cache-release sequence after successful resume in the same request, preserving phase receipts on success; explicit clear remains available. Cleanup does not change weights, committed version or pause and is excluded from activation phase timings.
- **Pause/cache controls:** update accepts `flush_cache=True` and `abort_all_requests=False`, preserves a caller-owned pause, and records the model label before opening generation admission. A retained or failed pause is not reported as a completed resume interval.
- **Preparation:** validate manifest/byte contracts, read/hash into shared tmpfs and decode/copy into private rank HOST_NUMA arenas while serving. `GPU_DELTA_HOST_CACHE_DIR` remains a deployment control and must name host-shared tmpfs (default `/dev/shm/sglang-gpu-delta-<uid>`). Build byte descriptors and prepare three fixed access-family kernels before PREPARED; dimensions/activity do not specialize code. Packed, word-affine and byte-affine layouts use generic addressing.
- **Fixed pipeline:** one hardware-DE stream, one Triton apply stream and exactly two decoded output slots. Decode-ready and apply-finished events order each slot's reuse; sticky status guards subsequent mutation. Output storage allocates after the pause/fence, while prepared descriptors and retained capacity avoid rebuilding the plan. The streams drain before release on error/cancellation. This is a fixed design, with no pipeline-depth selector, encoded-HBM ring, software decompression fallback or runtime autotuning. [Layout](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/23ae75c70a97c29cb5fcf919bb8c4d3c7c5057c2/python/sglang/srt/weight_sync/gpu_delta/layout.py), [codec](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/23ae75c70a97c29cb5fcf919bb8c4d3c7c5057c2/python/sglang/srt/weight_sync/gpu_delta/codec.py).
- **Device ownership:** only hardware-DE-facing tensors use feature-owned `cuMemAlloc`; aliases retain the allocation owner and producer/consumer streams drain before free. CUDA context restoration and uncertain-free diagnostics remain explicit. Model parameters are updated in place, with no concurrent unrelated updater.
- **Integrity:** publications carry codec/frame geometry, plan/stream/version bindings, matrix XOR or raw overwrite and omitted zero masks. Each update controls payload SHA verification with `validate_payload_hash=True` by default; `False` skips payload passes only. This request field is SGLang's sole hash-policy input. Manifest/file/native checks remain. Ordinary updates are consecutive; a fresh engine can accept HF base0→current.
- **Tracing:** [`SGLANG_ENABLE_NVTX_OPERATIONS=1`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/23ae75c70a97c29cb5fcf919bb8c4d3c7c5057c2/python/sglang/srt/weight_sync/gpu_delta/profiling.py) enables preparation, scheduler, worker and enqueue ranges. Disabled decorators return the callable unchanged; no added device sync. The benchmark owns capture; pause ranges close only on successful unpause.
- **Upstream interfaces:** tokenizer controls use the total replica × attention-DP rank count. DeepSeek canonical aliases and shared-expert mapping are resolved at admission. MXFP4 updates the shuffled inference scale images; retained loader-only checkpoint scales are outside the exclusive GPU-delta consumer path. TRTLLM/MegaMoE identity checks track the current layer-owned calibration buffers.
- **Versions:** each rollout/eval pool owns a consecutive transport sequence. The actor's model version is a separate label attached to generated samples; resume records it before generation admission. Repeated, jumped or rewound model labels do not change transport sequencing. Checkpoint reuse binds both rollout ID and model version.
- **W&B metrics:** [`perf/gpu_delta/*`](https://github.com/radixark/miles/blob/ca1a0df808747a729f2c8100a89b6cf49f5a5908/miles/backends/training_utils/weight_update/protocols/gpu_delta/metrics.py) reports completed updates, including a final update without a later train call; eval adds `eval/`. Rank timings use min/p50/max only with complete coverage. Shared encoded caches count once per engine/host; private DE arenas count per rank. Initial sync is logged without inventing a rollout step. Reporting errors cannot retry an applied update. No extra collective, polling or device synchronization is added for reporting. Engine prepare/apply/resume/activation metrics now use server tokenizer monotonic spans, excluding optional clear; outer coordinator activation remains the Miles await. Rank preparation and scheduler-pause clocks are unchanged.

| Publication | Inner GPU compression / hardware decode | Outer compression | Receiver preparation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `snappy-zstd` | Snappy | GPU Zstd, 1 MiB chunks | CPU Zstd into private rank DE arena |
| `lz4-zstd` | LZ4 | GPU Zstd, 1 MiB chunks | CPU Zstd into private rank DE arena |
| `lz4` | LZ4 | None | Copy compact inner arena into private rank DE arena |

### Admitted FlashInfer layouts

[Admission-time layout helpers](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/23ae75c70a97c29cb5fcf919bb8c4d3c7c5057c2/python/sglang/srt/weight_sync/gpu_delta/flashinfer.py) factor existing packed buffers into segmented affine byte views. Segments preserve canonical order and exclude padding; aliases receive one XOR, independent consumer images each receive it. Updates perform no weight/mask permutation or requantization.

| Native format | TRTLLM / routed | CuTe DSL | MegaMoE |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | Yes | — | — |
| FP8, 128×128 blocks, UE8M0 scales | Yes | — | — |
| MXFP8 | Yes | — | Yes |
| MXFP4 with MXFP8 activation | Yes | — | Yes |
| NVFP4 | W4A4 | W4A4 / W4A16 | W4A4 |

Only these combinations are admitted. This is native byte-layout support, not new inference kernels or full-serving qualification of every combination. Block128 UE8M0 accepts exact compact U8 scales and expands them losslessly into the consumer’s FP32 API image; arbitrary FP32 scales and load-time quantization/conversion fallbacks are rejected. CuTe wrappers/derived buffers must already exist. Routed experts require fixed topology and expert TP=1; EPLB, redundant experts and elastic joiners are unsupported. Full-serving evidence here remains **GLM-5.2 NVFP4 W4A16**.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Validation scope

Eight B300s; exact commits/image/digest below. **246 passed, zero failures/errors/skips** (63 SGLang controls including three topology cases; 157 Miles session/client/recovery/metrics; 26 CUDA/native). Actual imports and 13,728 files/modes verified before/after; originals closed, GPUs idle; both lint/format suites passed. Exact image/digest and source hashes are below.

Matrix132 is historical; not rerun for this source.

The initial 132 process-tree CPU attempt exceeded perf-FD capacity (1,121,792 required / 1,048,576 hard limit); system-wide collection supplied coverage. Exact warnings remain above. - Qualified workload: GLM-5.2 NVFP4 W4A16 on Blackwell with static MTP exclusions; no broader backend/precision claim.
- Dedicated-eval five-layer E2E is **skipped**: the eight-GPU training/rollout setup cannot host an extra eval engine. Unit/native pool checks are separate.

detail.body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Apply canonical Miles updates directly to live SGLang weights, and load HF-base delta publications on fresh or restarted engines. Paired [Miles #3894](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3894); [tracker #3734](https://github.com/radixark/miles/issues/3734).

## Modifications

- **Lifecycle/API:** four Miles-facing routes: `/get_gpu_delta_info`, `/update_weights_from_gpu_delta`, `/get_gpu_delta_status` and `/clear_gpu_delta_state`. One update carries the negotiated participants, session ID and publication descriptor. Tokenizer initialization and worker-count admission run once at the public request boundary. SGLang prepares while serving, then owns pause/fence/apply, all-rank acknowledgement and resume. APPLIED IPC carries identity/provenance/state/pause boundaries and the applied/target-version verdict; full metrics remain in RESUMED and status. Internal preparation failure is released; an uncertain XOR after apply dispatch is never replayed.
- **Recovery/deployment:** rolling and fresh-engine HF-base updates share the explicit descriptor contract; there is no manifest-only loader. Resources remain cached by default (`release_state=False`). `release_state=True` performs the existing all-rank close/shared-cache-release sequence after successful resume in the same request, preserving phase receipts on success; explicit clear remains available. Cleanup does not change weights, committed version or pause and is excluded from activation phase timings.
- **Pause/cache controls:** update accepts `flush_cache=True` and `abort_all_requests=False`, preserves a caller-owned pause, and records the model label before opening generation admission. A retained or failed pause is not reported as a completed resume interval.
- **Preparation:** validate manifest/byte contracts, read/hash into shared tmpfs and decode/copy into private rank HOST_NUMA arenas while serving. `GPU_DELTA_HOST_CACHE_DIR` remains a deployment control and must name host-shared tmpfs (default `/dev/shm/sglang-gpu-delta-<uid>`). Build byte descriptors and prepare three fixed access-family kernels before PREPARED; dimensions/activity do not specialize code. Packed, word-affine and byte-affine layouts use generic addressing.
- **Fixed pipeline:** one hardware-DE stream, one Triton apply stream and exactly two decoded output slots. Decode-ready and apply-finished events order each slot's reuse; sticky status guards subsequent mutation. Output storage allocates after the pause/fence, while prepared descriptors and retained capacity avoid rebuilding the plan. The streams drain before release on error/cancellation. This is a fixed design, with no pipeline-depth selector, encoded-HBM ring, software decompression fallback or runtime autotuning. [Layout](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/23ae75c70a97c29cb5fcf919bb8c4d3c7c5057c2/python/sglang/srt/weight_sync/gpu_delta/layout.py), [codec](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/23ae75c70a97c29cb5fcf919bb8c4d3c7c5057c2/python/sglang/srt/weight_sync/gpu_delta/codec.py).
- **Device ownership:** only hardware-DE-facing tensors use feature-owned `cuMemAlloc`; aliases retain the allocation owner and producer/consumer streams drain before free. CUDA context restoration and uncertain-free diagnostics remain explicit. Model parameters are updated in place, with no concurrent unrelated updater.
- **Integrity:** publications carry codec/frame geometry, plan/stream/version bindings, matrix XOR or raw overwrite and omitted zero masks. Each update controls payload SHA verification with `validate_payload_hash=True` by default; `False` skips payload passes only. This request field is SGLang's sole hash-policy input. Manifest/file/native checks remain. Ordinary updates are consecutive; a fresh engine can accept HF base0→current.
- **Tracing:** [`SGLANG_ENABLE_NVTX_OPERATIONS=1`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/23ae75c70a97c29cb5fcf919bb8c4d3c7c5057c2/python/sglang/srt/weight_sync/gpu_delta/profiling.py) enables preparation, scheduler, worker and enqueue ranges. Disabled decorators return the callable unchanged; no added device sync. The benchmark owns capture; pause ranges close only on successful unpause.
- **Upstream interfaces:** tokenizer controls use the total replica × attention-DP rank count. DeepSeek canonical aliases and shared-expert mapping are resolved at admission. MXFP4 updates the shuffled inference scale images; retained loader-only checkpoint scales are outside the exclusive GPU-delta consumer path. TRTLLM/MegaMoE identity checks track the current layer-owned calibration buffers.
- **Versions:** each rollout/eval pool owns a consecutive transport sequence. The actor's model version is a separate label attached to generated samples; resume records it before generation admission. Repeated, jumped or rewound model labels do not change transport sequencing. Checkpoint reuse binds both rollout ID and model version.
- **W&B metrics:** [`perf/gpu_delta/*`](https://github.com/radixark/miles/blob/ca1a0df808747a729f2c8100a89b6cf49f5a5908/miles/backends/training_utils/weight_update/protocols/gpu_delta/metrics.py) reports completed updates, including a final update without a later train call; eval adds `eval/`. Rank timings use min/p50/max only with complete coverage. Shared encoded caches count once per engine/host; private DE arenas count per rank. Initial sync is logged without inventing a rollout step. Reporting errors cannot retry an applied update. No extra collective, polling or device synchronization is added for reporting. Engine prepare/apply/resume/activation metrics now use server tokenizer monotonic spans, excluding optional clear; outer coordinator activation remains the Miles await. Rank preparation and scheduler-pause clocks are unchanged.

| Publication | Inner GPU compression / hardware decode | Outer compression | Receiver preparation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `snappy-zstd` | Snappy | GPU Zstd, 1 MiB chunks | CPU Zstd into private rank DE arena |
| `lz4-zstd` | LZ4 | GPU Zstd, 1 MiB chunks | CPU Zstd into private rank DE arena |

### Admitted FlashInfer layouts

+
+"""Prepared groups of byte-affine XOR destinations; imported only at admission."""
+
+import math
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from functools import lru_cache, partial
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+BLOCK = 2048
+ELEMENTS = 512
+WARPS = 4
+RESIDENT_WAVES = 4
+MAX_AXES = 64
+_INT64_MAX = (1 << 63) - 1
+_MAX_TILES = (1 << 31) - 1
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None, typed=True)
+def _resident_ctas(kernel, device_index):
+    """One resource-residency wave, cached per loaded kernel and CUDA device."""
+    from cuda.bindings import driver
+
+    with torch.cuda.device(device_index):
+        status, blocks = driver.cuOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(
+            driver.CUfunction(int(kernel.function)),
+            kernel.metadata.num_warps * 32,
+            kernel.metadata.shared,
+        )
+        if status != driver.CUresult.CUDA_SUCCESS or blocks <= 0:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"CUDA occupancy query failed: status={status}, blocks={blocks}"
+            )
+        return (
+            blocks
+            * torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device_index).multi_processor_count
+        )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _check_decode(
+    statuses, actual_sizes, expected_sizes, error, count, BLOCK: tl.constexpr
+):
+    index = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    active = index < count
+    status = tl.load(statuses + index, active, other=0)
+    actual = tl.load(actual_sizes + index, active, other=0)
+    expected = tl.load(expected_sizes + index, active, other=0)
+    if tl.sum(((status != 0) | (actual != expected)).to(tl.int32), 0) != 0:
+        tl.atomic_or(error, 1)
+
+
+def prepare_status_check(decoder, error):
+    """Prepare metadata-only validation; the returned call enqueues on apply."""
+    count = decoder.statuses.numel()
+    arguments = (
+        decoder.statuses,
+        decoder.actual_sizes,
+        decoder.expected_sizes,
+        error,
+        count,
+    )
+    grid = (triton.cdiv(count, 1024), 1, 1)
+    kernel = _check_decode.warmup(*arguments, 1024, grid=grid, num_warps=4)
+    _ = kernel.run
+    return partial(kernel[grid], *arguments)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _scalar_quotient(numerator, denominator):
+    # Runtime scalar row/base division: never narrow a large coordinate or axis.
+    if numerator <= 0xFFFFFFFF:
+        if denominator > 0xFFFFFFFF:
+            quotient = tl.full((), 0, tl.int64)
+        else:
+            quotient = (numerator.to(tl.uint32) // denominator.to(tl.uint32)).to(
+                tl.int64
+            )
+    else:
+        quotient = numerator // denominator
+    return quotient
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _affine_offset(index, metadata, shape, stride, axes):
+    offset = tl.full(index.shape, 0, tl.int64)
+    rest = index
+    axis = axes - 1
+    while axis > 0:
+        length = tl.load(metadata + shape + axis)
+        step = tl.load(metadata + stride + axis)
+        quotient = _scalar_quotient(rest, length)
+        offset += (rest - quotient * length) * step
+        rest = quotient
+        axis -= 1
+    return offset + rest * tl.load(metadata + stride)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _affine_lanes(base, delta, metadata, shape, stride, axes, MAX_DELTA: tl.constexpr):
+    offset = tl.full(delta.shape, 0, tl.int64)
+    axis = axes - 1
+    while axis > 0:
+        length = tl.load(metadata + shape + axis)
+        step = tl.load(metadata + stride + axis)
+        quotient = _scalar_quotient(base, length)
+        remainder = base - quotient * length
+        if length > MAX_DELTA:
+            lane_quotient = tl.full(delta.shape, 0, tl.uint32)
+            lane_remainder = delta
+        else:
+            lane_quotient = delta // length.to(tl.uint32)
+            lane_remainder = delta - lane_quotient * length.to(tl.uint32)
+        # b=qL+r, d=aL+t => coordinate=r+t-cL, next flat=q+a+c.
+        # 0<=t<L gives a single carry; the new delta a+c never exceeds d.
+        # Group subtraction before addition to avoid an overflowing r+t when
+        # a valid axis approaches INT64_MAX. Only bounded deltas use uint32.
+        carry = (lane_remainder.to(tl.int64) >= length - remainder).to(tl.uint32)
+        coordinate = remainder + (
+            lane_remainder.to(tl.int64) - carry.to(tl.int64) * length
+        )
+        offset += coordinate * step
+        base = quotient
+        delta = lane_quotient + carry
+        axis -= 1
+    return offset + (base + delta.to(tl.int64)) * tl.load(metadata + stride)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _load_source(
+    source,
+    metadata,
+    shape,
+    axes,
+    mode,
+    base,
+    size,
+    WORD: tl.constexpr,
+    ELEMENTS: tl.constexpr,
+    ALIGNMENT: tl.constexpr,
+    PACKED: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    lanes = tl.arange(0, ELEMENTS)
+    index = base + lanes * WORD
+    mask = index < size
+    # Keep the actual memory operations in the uniform access-mode branches.
+    # Merging an arbitrary affine offset before a common load loses the
+    # contiguous branch's vector-address proof. Only base has a fixed multiple;
+    # arbitrary outer strides in row/affine mappings keep their true alignment.
+    if mode == 1:
+        offset = tl.multiple_of(base // WORD, ELEMENTS) + lanes
+        value = tl.load(source + offset, mask, other=0)
+    elif PACKED or mode == 2:
+        if PACKED:
+            start = _packed_row_start(base, metadata, shape, ELEMENTS * WORD)
+        else:
+            start = _affine_offset(base, metadata, shape, shape + axes, axes)
+        start = tl.multiple_of(start // WORD, ALIGNMENT // WORD)
+        value = tl.load(source + start + lanes, mask, other=0)
+    else:
+        offset = _affine_lanes(
+            base,
+            (lanes * WORD).to(tl.uint32),
+            metadata,
+            shape,
+            shape + axes,
+            axes,
+            (ELEMENTS - 1) * WORD,
+        )
+        value = tl.load(source + offset // WORD, mask, other=0)
+    return value
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _xor_target(
+    target,
+    value,
+    metadata,
+    shape,
+    axes,
+    mode,
+    base,
+    size,
+    WORD: tl.constexpr,
+    ELEMENTS: tl.constexpr,
+    ALIGNMENT: tl.constexpr,
+    PACKED: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    lanes = tl.arange(0, ELEMENTS)
+    index = base + lanes * WORD
+    mask = index < size
+    if mode == 1:
+        offset = tl.multiple_of(base // WORD, ELEMENTS) + lanes
+        previous = tl.load(target + offset, mask, other=0)
+        tl.store(target + offset, value ^ previous, mask)
+    elif PACKED or mode == 2:
+        if PACKED:
+            start = _packed_row_start(base, metadata, shape, ELEMENTS * WORD)
+        else:
+            start = _affine_offset(base, metadata, shape, shape + axes, axes)
+        start = tl.multiple_of(start // WORD, ALIGNMENT // WORD)
+        offset = start + lanes
+        previous = tl.load(target + offset, mask, other=0)
+        tl.store(target + offset, value ^ previous, mask)
+    else:
+        offset = (
+            _affine_lanes(
+                base,
+                (lanes * WORD).to(tl.uint32),
+                metadata,
+                shape,
+                shape + axes,
+                axes,
+                (ELEMENTS - 1) * WORD,
+            )
+            // WORD
+        )
+        previous = tl.load(target + offset, mask, other=0)
+        tl.store(target + offset, value ^ previous, mask)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _packed_row_start(base, metadata, shape, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    # Packed row contracts are exactly two axes; contiguous sides bypass this.
+    # Active total tiles <= INT32_MAX and the inner row is BLOCK-divisible.
+    # Keep only tile division uint32; byte coordinates/strides remain int64.
+    inner = tl.load(metadata + shape + 1)
+    outer_stride = tl.load(metadata + shape + 2)
+    tile = (base // BLOCK).to(tl.uint32)
+    row_tiles = (inner // BLOCK).to(tl.uint32)
+    row = (tile // row_tiles).to(tl.int64)
+    return row * outer_stride + (base - row * inner)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _apply_record(
+    pointers,
+    metadata,
+    record,
+    tile,
+    tile_stride,
+    WORD: tl.constexpr,
+    ALIGNMENT: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    FAMILY: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    size = tl.load(metadata + record)
+    source_mode = tl.load(metadata + record + 1)
+    target_mode = tl.load(metadata + record + 2)
+    count = tl.load(metadata + record + 6)
+    position = tl.load(metadata + record + 7)
+    first = tl.load(metadata + record + 8)
+    end = tl.load(metadata + record + 9)
+    axes = tl.load(metadata + record + 10)
+    # Active contracts have at most INT32_MAX tiles by admission. Only byte
+    # offsets/affine coordinates need int64; variable tile division uses uint32.
+    per_item = tl.cdiv(size, BLOCK).to(tl.uint32)
+    DTYPE: tl.constexpr = tl.uint32 if WORD == 4 else tl.uint8
+    ELEMENTS: tl.constexpr = 512
+    # A CTA may visit several tiles of this group. Keep record selection and
+    # scalar geometry outside that loop, then search again only across END.
+    while tile < end:
+        local = (tile - first).to(tl.uint32)
+        item = local // per_item
+        base = (local - item * per_item).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK
+        source = tl.multiple_of(tl.load(pointers + position + item), ALIGNMENT).to(
+            tl.pointer_type(DTYPE)
+        )
+        target = tl.multiple_of(
+            tl.load(pointers + position + count + item), ALIGNMENT
+        ).to(tl.pointer_type(DTYPE))
+        shape = record + 11
+        if FAMILY == 1:
+            # This family's coordinate descriptors are uint32-word based.
+            # CPU preparation validates/classifies the original byte contract;
+            # size/tile accounting stays byte-based. The source is contiguous.
+            lanes = tl.arange(0, ELEMENTS)
+            index = tl.multiple_of(base // 4, ELEMENTS) + lanes
+            target_shape = shape + 2 * axes
+            offset = _affine_lanes(
+                base // 4,
+                lanes.to(tl.uint32),
+                metadata,
+                target_shape,
+                target_shape + axes,
+                axes,
+                ELEMENTS - 1,
+            )
+            mask = base + lanes * 4 < size
+            value = tl.load(source + index, mask, other=0)
+            previous = tl.load(target + offset, mask, other=0)
+            tl.store(target + offset, value ^ previous, mask)
+        else:
+            # Keep loads/stores inside their uniform access-mode branches:
+            # merging row starts first loses the contiguous address proof.
+            # Packed WORD4 uses one subtile; general byte fallback uses four.
+            part = 0
+            while part < 4 // WORD:
+                subbase = base + part * ELEMENTS * WORD
+                value = _load_source(
+                    source,
+                    metadata,
+                    shape,
+                    axes,
+                    source_mode,
+                    subbase,
+                    size,
+                    WORD,
+                    ELEMENTS,
+                    ALIGNMENT,
+                    FAMILY == 0,
+                )
+                _xor_target(
+                    target,
+                    value,
+                    metadata,
+                    shape + 2 * axes,
+                    axes,
+                    target_mode,
+                    subbase,
+                    size,
+                    WORD,
+                    ELEMENTS,
+                    ALIGNMENT,
+                    FAMILY == 0,
+                )
+                part += 1
+        tile += tile_stride
+    return tile
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _xor_batch(pointers, metadata, error, BLOCK: tl.constexpr, FAMILY: tl.constexpr):
+    # No pointer or model access may precede the sticky decode-status gate.
+    if tl.load(error) == 0:
+        tile = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+        tile_stride = tl.num_programs(0).to(tl.int64)
+        groups = tl.load(metadata)
+        total = tl.load(metadata + groups)  # final END; metadata[0] is0 if empty
+        while tile < total:
+            low = tl.full((), 0, tl.int64)
+            high = groups
+            # First cumulative END greater than tile. Empty groups are skipped.
+            while low < high:
+                middle = (low + high) // 2
+                end = tl.load(metadata + 1 + middle)
+                if tile < end:
+                    high = middle
+                else:
+                    low = middle + 1
+            record = tl.load(metadata + 1 + groups + low)
+            word = tl.load(metadata + record + 5)
+            if FAMILY != 2 or word == 4:
+                source_alignment = tl.load(metadata + record + 3)
+                target_alignment = tl.load(metadata + record + 4)
+                if (source_alignment >= 16) & (target_alignment >= 16):
+                    tile = _apply_record(
+                        pointers,
+                        metadata,
+                        record,
+                        tile,
+                        tile_stride,
+                        4,
+                        16,
+                        BLOCK,
+                        FAMILY,
+                    )
+                else:
+                    tile = _apply_record(
+                        pointers,
+                        metadata,
+                        record,
+                        tile,
+                        tile_stride,
+                        4,
+                        4,
+                        BLOCK,
+                        FAMILY,
+                    )
+            else:
+                tile = _apply_record(
+                    pointers, metadata, record, tile, tile_stride, 1, 1, BLOCK, FAMILY
+                )
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None, typed=True)
+def _compiled(device_index, family):
+    """Three fixed access families per device, all loaded before pause."""
+    if (
+        type(device_index) is not int
+        or not 0 <= device_index < torch.cuda.device_count()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("invalid GPU delta apply device")
+    if type(family) is not int or family not in (0, 1, 2):
+        raise ValueError("invalid GPU delta apply family")
+    with torch.cuda.device(device_index):
+        kernel = _xor_batch.warmup(
+            torch.int64,
+            torch.int64,
+            torch.int32,
+            BLOCK,
+            family,
+            grid=(1, 1, 1),
+            num_warps=WARPS,
+        )
+        _ = kernel.run
+        _resident_ctas(kernel, device_index)
+        return kernel
+
+
+def _normalize(shape, stride):
+    """Keep the same flat element mapping with fewer affine axes."""
+    axes = []
+    for size, step in reversed(tuple(zip(shape, stride))):
+        if size == 1:
+            continue
+        if axes and step == axes[-1][0] * axes[-1][1]:
+            axes[-1] = (size * axes[-1][0], axes[-1][1])
+        else:
+            axes.append((size, step))
+    if not axes:
+        return (1,), (1,)
+    shape, stride = zip(*reversed(axes))
+    return shape, stride
+
+
+def _access_mode(shape, stride, block):
+    """Classify normalized byte geometry without model or format dimensions.
+
+    0: arbitrary affine coordinates; each lane computes its runtime byte offset.
+    1: contiguous bytes; flat logical and physical offsets are identical.
+    2: contiguous innermost rows whose lengths are block-divisible, so a tile
+       cannot cross a row boundary; only the tile's row start needs remapping.
+    """
+    if stride == (1,):
+        return 1
+    return 2 if stride[-1] == 1 and shape[-1] % block == 0 else 0
+
+
+def _word_bytes(contract, alignment):
+    size, ss, st, ts, tt = contract
+    aligned_rows = all(
+        stride[-1] == 1
+        and shape[-1] % 4 == 0
+        and all(n == 1 or step % 4 == 0 for n, step in zip(shape[:-1], stride[:-1]))
+        for shape, stride in ((ss, st), (ts, tt))
+    )
+    return 4 if size % 4 == 0 and min(alignment) >= 4 and aligned_rows else 1
+
+
+def _row_alignment(shape, stride, alignment):
+    if _access_mode(shape, stride, BLOCK) != 2:
+        return alignment
+    # The inner row coordinate is BLOCK aligned. Include every active outer
+    # stride so a16B base pointer never overstates a4B-aligned row start.
+    return math.gcd(
+        alignment, *(step for n, step in zip(shape[:-1], stride[:-1]) if n > 1)
+    )
+
+
+def _validate_contract(contract, count):
+    size, ss, st, ts, tt = contract
+    if (
+        type(count) is not int
+        or not 0 <= count <= _INT64_MAX
+        or type(size) is not int
+        or not 0 < size <= _INT64_MAX
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("invalid GPU delta apply size/count")
+    for shape, stride in ((ss, st), (ts, tt)):
+        if not 1 <= len(shape) <= MAX_AXES or len(shape) != len(stride):
+            raise ValueError("unsupported GPU delta affine axis count")

+        if (
+            self.source.shape != self.destination.shape
+            or self.source.dtype != self.destination.dtype
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported derived delta buffer geometry: {self.name}")
+
+    @cached_property
+    def source_pointer(self):
+        return self.source.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+
+
+def _tensor_identity(tensor):
+    return (
+        tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr(),
+        tensor.storage_offset(),
+        tuple(tensor.shape),
+        tuple(tensor.stride()),
+        tensor.dtype,
+        tensor.device,
+    )
+
+
+def dense_target(name, meta, module, target, slices):
+    quant_name = type(getattr(module, "quant_method", None)).__name__
+    if quant_name not in {
+        "NoneType",
+        "UnquantizedLinearMethod",
+        "UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod",
+    }:
+        raise ValueError(f"unsupported dense delta quantization {quant_name}: {name}")
+    if tuple(target.shape) != tuple(stop - start for start, stop in slices):
+        if hasattr(module, "shard_indices"):
+            indices = module.shard_indices
+            if indices.num_added_elements:
+                raise ValueError("added-vocabulary delta layout is not supported")
+            start, stop = indices.org_vocab_start_index, indices.org_vocab_end_index
+            slices[0] = [start, stop]
+            target = target[: stop - start]
+        else:
+            mismatches = [
+                i
+                for i, (local, full) in enumerate(zip(target.shape, meta["shape"]))
+                if local != full
+            ]
+            if len(mismatches) != 1 or len(target.shape) != len(meta["shape"]):
+                raise ValueError(f"unclassified dense shape mapping: {name}")
+            dim = mismatches[0]
+            allowed_dim = (
+                getattr(target, "input_dim", None)
+                if type(module).__name__ == "RowParallelLinear"
+                else getattr(target, "output_dim", None)
+            )
+            if dim != allowed_dim or not hasattr(module, "tp_group"):
+                raise ValueError(f"unclassified tensor-parallel mapping: {name}")
+            from sglang.srt.distributed.utils import get_group_rank_size
+
+            rank, _ = get_group_rank_size(module.tp_group)
+            size = target.shape[dim]
+            slices[dim] = [rank * size, (rank + 1) * size]
+    return target, slices
+
+
+class ConsumerSnapshot:
+    """Read live consumer fields without retaining a stale replacement tensor."""
+
+    def __init__(self, read):
+        self.read = read
+        self.objects = read()
+        self.tensors = [
+            (index, _tensor_identity(value))
+            for index, value in enumerate(self.objects)
+            if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor)
+        ]
+
+    def check_objects(self):
+        current = self.read()
+        if len(current) != len(self.objects) or any(
+            a is not b for a, b in zip(current, self.objects)
+        ):
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "GPU delta consumer storage changed; readmission required"
+            )
+
+    def check(self):
+        self.check_objects()
+        if any(
+            _tensor_identity(self.objects[index]) != expected
+            for index, expected in self.tensors
+        ):
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "GPU delta consumer storage changed; readmission required"
+            )
+
+
+def gate_up_target(target, module, shard, slices):
+    from sglang.srt.distributed.utils import get_group_rank_size
+
+    rank, _ = get_group_rank_size(module.tp_group)
+    dim = target.output_dim
+    half = target.shape[dim] // 2
+    target = target.narrow(dim, shard * half, half)
+    slices[dim] = [rank * half, (rank + 1) * half]
+    return target
+
+
+class ParameterBindings:
+    """Shared routed-expert and ordinary dense binding context at admission."""
+
+    def __init__(self, model, stacked_params=()):
+        self.modules = dict(model.named_modules())
+        self.params = dict(model.named_parameters(remove_duplicate=False))
+        self.gate_up_params = [
+            (source, shard)
+            for target, source, shard in stacked_params
+            if target == "gate_up_proj"
+        ]
+        self.excluded = {}
+        self.moe_layers = {}
+        self.moe_layouts = {}
+
+    def bind(self, name, meta, target_name, target=None):
+        if meta["dtype"] not in _DTYPES.values():
+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported canonical dtype for {name}: {meta['dtype']}")
+        match = re.fullmatch(
+            r"(.+\.experts)\.(\d+)\.(gate|up|down)_proj\.(.+)", target_name
+        )
+        if match:
+            prefix, expert, projection, suffix = match.groups()
+            layer = self.modules.get(prefix)
+            if layer is None:
+                raise ValueError(f"canonical expert has no runtime layer: {name}")
+            if prefix not in self.moe_layers:
+                if layer.moe_tp_size != 1 or layer.use_presharded_weights:
+                    raise ValueError(
+                        "GPU delta requires expert TP=1 and an unsharded canonical checkpoint"
+                    )
+                self.moe_layouts[prefix] = _identify_moe_layout(layer)
+                self.moe_layers[prefix] = layer
+            binding = _moe_binding(
+                name,
+                meta,
+                layer,
+                int(expert),
+                projection,
+                suffix,
+                self.moe_layouts[prefix],
+            )
+            if binding is None:
+                self.excluded[name] = (
+                    "static activation calibration"
+                    if suffix == "input_scale"
+                    else "expert owned by another EP rank"
+                )
+            return binding
+        if target is None:
+            target = self.params.get(target_name)
+        slices = _full_slices(meta["shape"])
+        if target is None:
+            for source_stem, shard in self.gate_up_params:
+                if source_stem not in target_name or ".experts." in target_name:
+                    continue
+                candidate = target_name.replace(source_stem, "gate_up_proj")
+                target = self.params.get(candidate)
+                if target is None:
+                    continue
+                module = self.modules[candidate.rsplit(".", 1)[0]]
+                target = gate_up_target(target, module, shard, slices)
+                target_name = candidate
+                break
+        if target is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"unclassified canonical tensor: {name}")
+        module = self.modules[target_name.rsplit(".", 1)[0]]
+        target, slices = dense_target(name, meta, module, target, slices)
+        return _direct_binding(name, meta, target, slices)

+"""Canonical metadata for the GPU-delta receiver's immutable startup checkpoint.
+
+Read only at first delta admission. The exclusive controller must keep the
+original local checkpoint unchanged for the engine's lifetime; this is metadata
+discovery, not proof of the current model's weight values. Ordinary loaders and
+model methods are never modified.
+"""
+
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from safetensors import safe_open
+
+
+def read_canonical_checkpoint_inventory(model_runner):
+    """Read source names, shapes and dtypes without materializing any tensors.
+
+    The source inventory is independent of quantization. Runtime layout admission
+    checks the physical buffers and model mappings separately.
+    """
+    from sglang.srt.model_loader.loader import DefaultModelLoader, ModelOptModelLoader
+    from sglang.srt.model_loader.weight_utils import (
+        filter_duplicate_safetensors_files,
+        maybe_add_mtp_safetensors,
+    )
+
+    model = model_runner.model
+    config = model_runner.load_config
+    model_config = model_runner.model_config
+    loader = model_runner.loader
+    # ModelOpt's already-quantized branch delegates to DefaultModelLoader.
+    # Subclasses may override the iterator or transform its names and values.
+    if type(loader) not in (DefaultModelLoader, ModelOptModelLoader):
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta requires the standard local checkpoint loader")
+    if type(loader) is ModelOptModelLoader and not model_config._is_already_quantized():
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta does not support load-time ModelOpt conversion")
+    if config.load_format not in {"auto", "safetensors", "fastsafetensors"}:
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta requires a standard safetensors load format")
+    if model_runner.is_draft_worker or config.draft_model_idx is not None:
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta checkpoint admission requires the target model")
+    if (
+        getattr(model, "secondary_weights", ())
+        or getattr(model, "allow_patterns_overrides", None) is not None
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta does not support secondary or remapped sources")
+    if config.decryption_key_file is not None:
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta does not support encrypted checkpoint sources")
+
+    folder = Path(model_config.model_path)
+    if not folder.is_dir():
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta requires the original immutable local checkpoint")
+    # Match the default loader's primary source (empty prefix, no draft remap).
+    # Reuse its index filtering and bundled-MTP rules without invoking downloads,
+    # checksum verification, tensor loading, or checkpoint page-cache prefetch.
+    files = filter_duplicate_safetensors_files(
+        [str(path) for path in folder.glob("*.safetensors")],
+        str(folder),
+        "model.safetensors.index.json",
+    )
+    files = maybe_add_mtp_safetensors(
+        files, str(folder), "model.safetensors.index.json", model_config.hf_config
+    )
+    if not files:
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta checkpoint has no selected safetensors shards")
+    return _read_headers(files)
+
+
+def _read_headers(files):
+    inventory = {}
+    for path in files:
+        with safe_open(path, framework="pt", device="cpu") as source:
+            for name in source.keys():  # noqa: SIM118 - safe_open is not iterable.
+                if name in inventory:
+                    raise ValueError(f"ambiguous canonical checkpoint tensor: {name}")
+                tensor_slice = source.get_slice(name)
+                inventory[name] = {
+                    "shape": tensor_slice.get_shape(),
+                    "dtype": tensor_slice.get_dtype(),
+                }
+    if not inventory:
+        raise ValueError("canonical checkpoint metadata is empty")
+    return inventory

+"""Caller-owned nvCOMP decoding for direct weight deltas.
+
+Preparation allocates small metadata and workspace; decoded output slots are bound
+only after generation pauses.
+The hot path calls the public C API directly: no nvCOMP Python array finalizers,
+implicit size discovery, host scalar reads or wrapper-added synchronization.
+The nvCOMP DE backend may wait for earlier work on the calling stream before
+submitting decompression, even though the public API is named Async.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ctypes
+import importlib.metadata
+import os
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta import profiling
+
+
+class _SnappyOptions(ctypes.Structure):
+    _fields_ = [
+        ("backend", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("sort_before_hw_decompress", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("reserved", ctypes.c_char * 56),
+    ]
+
+
+class _Lz4Options(ctypes.Structure):
+    _fields_ = [
+        ("backend", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("sort_before_hw_decompress", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("data_type", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("bitshuffle_mode", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("reserved", ctypes.c_char * 48),
+    ]
+
+
+_DECOMPRESS_OPTIONS = {
+    "snappy": ("Snappy", _SnappyOptions),
+    "lz4": ("LZ4", _Lz4Options),
+}
+_MAX_FRAME_BYTES = 4 << 20
+_INT64_MAX = np.iinfo(np.int64).max
+
+
+def _require_hardware_device(device: torch.device, algorithm: str) -> int:
+    from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.memory import _driver
+
+    driver = _driver()
+    status, mask = driver.cuDeviceGetAttribute(
+        driver.CUdevice_attribute.CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MEM_DECOMPRESS_ALGORITHM_MASK,
+        device.index,
+    )
+    if status:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"GPU-delta DE device admission failed: CUDA {status}")
+    status, maximum = driver.cuDeviceGetAttribute(
+        driver.CUdevice_attribute.CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MEM_DECOMPRESS_MAXIMUM_LENGTH,
+        device.index,
+    )
+    if status:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"GPU-delta DE device admission failed: CUDA {status}")
+    algorithms = driver.CUmemDecompressAlgorithm
+    required = {
+        "Snappy": algorithms.CU_MEM_DECOMPRESS_ALGORITHM_SNAPPY,
+        "LZ4": algorithms.CU_MEM_DECOMPRESS_ALGORITHM_LZ4,
+    }[algorithm]
+    if not mask & required:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Device has no hardware {algorithm} decompressor")
+    if maximum <= 0:
+        raise RuntimeError("Device has no positive hardware decompression limit")
+    return maximum
+
+
+class _Alignments(ctypes.Structure):
+    _fields_ = [
+        ("input", ctypes.c_size_t),
+        ("output", ctypes.c_size_t),
+        ("temp", ctypes.c_size_t),
+    ]
+
+
+@dataclass
+class DecodeWorkspace:
+    temporary: torch.Tensor
+    actual_sizes: torch.Tensor
+    statuses: torch.Tensor
+
+
+class NvcompDecoder:
+    """One device's fixed inner-codec hardware decoder.
+
+    Missing libraries and unsupported hardware fail admission. There is no CPU
+    decoder, algorithm substitution or software fallback.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, device: torch.device, inner_codec: str):
+        self.device = torch.device(device)
+        if self.device.type != "cuda" or self.device.index is None:
+            raise ValueError("Delta decoder requires an explicit CUDA device")
+        if inner_codec not in _DECOMPRESS_OPTIONS:
+            raise ValueError("GPU delta inner codec must be snappy or lz4")
+        self.inner_codec = inner_codec
+        self._algorithm, options_type = _DECOMPRESS_OPTIONS[inner_codec]
+        sorting = os.environ.get("GPU_DELTA_SORT_BEFORE_HW_DECOMPRESS", "0")
+        if sorting not in {"0", "1"}:
+            raise ValueError("GPU_DELTA_SORT_BEFORE_HW_DECOMPRESS must be 0 or 1")
+        cuda_major = torch.version.cuda.split(".")[0]
+        package = f"nvidia-libnvcomp-cu{cuda_major}"
+        distribution = importlib.metadata.distribution(package)
+        version = tuple(int(v) for v in distribution.version.split(".")[:2])
+        if not (5, 3) <= version < (6, 0) or ctypes.sizeof(ctypes.c_size_t) != 8:
+            raise RuntimeError("Direct GPU deltas require the 64-bit nvCOMP 5.3+ ABI")
+        self.backend = "hardware"
+        self._options = options_type()
+        # Explicit backend selection: DEFAULT can silently select software.
+        self._options.backend = 1
+        self._options.sort_before_hw_decompress = int(sorting)
+        if self._algorithm == "LZ4":
+            self._options.data_type = 0  # NVCOMP_TYPE_CHAR
+            self._options.bitshuffle_mode = 0  # NVCOMP_BITSHUFFLE_NONE
+        self.maximum_chunk_bytes = _require_hardware_device(
+            self.device, self._algorithm
+        )
+        self._library = ctypes.CDLL(
+            str(distribution.locate_file("nvidia/libnvcomp/lib64/libnvcomp.so.5"))
+        )
+        pointer, size = ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t
+        self._temporary = self._bind(
+            "GetTempSizeAsync", [size, size, options_type, ctypes.POINTER(size), size]
+        )
+        required_alignments = self._bind(
+            "GetRequiredAlignments", [options_type, ctypes.POINTER(_Alignments)]
+        )
+        self._decode = self._bind(
+            "Async",
+            [
+                pointer,
+                pointer,
+                pointer,
+                pointer,
+                size,
+                pointer,
+                size,
+                pointer,
+                options_type,
+                pointer,
+                pointer,
+            ],
+        )
+        self.alignments = _Alignments()
+        self._check(required_alignments(self._options, ctypes.byref(self.alignments)))
+        self._temporary_sizes: dict[tuple[int, int, int], int] = {}
+
+    def _bind(self, suffix, arguments):
+        function = getattr(
+            self._library,
+            "nvcompBatched" + self._algorithm + "Decompress" + suffix,
+        )
+        function.argtypes, function.restype = arguments, ctypes.c_int
+        return function
+
+    def _check(self, status):
+        if status != 0:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"nvCOMP {self.inner_codec}/{self.backend} failed: status={status}"
+            )
+
+    def temporary_bytes(self, geometry: tuple[int, int, int]) -> int:
+        if not geometry[0]:
+            return 0
+        cached = self._temporary_sizes.get(geometry)
+        if cached is not None:
+            return cached
+        size = ctypes.c_size_t()
+        with torch.cuda.device(self.device):
+            self._check(
+                self._temporary(
+                    geometry[0],
+                    geometry[1],
+                    self._options,
+                    ctypes.byref(size),
+                    geometry[2],
+                )
+            )
+        self._temporary_sizes[geometry] = size.value
+        return size.value
+
+    def _allocate_workspace(self, geometry) -> DecodeWorkspace:
+        """One DE stream shares scratch; statuses/sizes belong to two slots."""
+        from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.memory import device_empty
+
+        maximum_count = max((batch[0] for batch in geometry), default=0)
+        temporary = max((self.temporary_bytes(batch) for batch in geometry), default=0)
+        workspace = DecodeWorkspace(
+            device_empty((temporary,), dtype=torch.uint8, device=self.device),
+            device_empty((2, maximum_count), dtype=torch.int64, device=self.device),
+            device_empty((2, maximum_count), dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device),
+        )
+        if temporary and workspace.temporary.data_ptr() % self.alignments.temp:
+            raise ValueError("Misaligned decoder workspace")
+        return workspace
+
+    def _frame_geometry(self, table, counts, input_base, input_bytes):
+        """Validate numeric rows and derive workspace/output bounds in one pass."""
+        if (
+            table.dtype != np.int64
+            or table.shape != (4, sum(counts))
+            or not table.flags.c_contiguous
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Expected contiguous int64(4,N) frame metadata")
+        if not 0 <= input_base <= _INT64_MAX - input_bytes:
+            raise ValueError("Input pointer arithmetic exceeds signed metadata")
+        bounds, remainders, geometry = [0, 0], [None, None], []
+        maximum = self.maximum_chunk_bytes
+        offset = 0
+        for index, count in enumerate(counts):
+            inputs, encoded, decoded, outputs = table[:, offset : offset + count]
+            offset += count
+            slot = index % 2
+            if not count:
+                geometry.append((0, 0, 0))
+                continue
+            # HARDWARE does not check oversized buffers. Check actual lengths,
+            # not the compressor's worst-case allocation: compressible 4 MiB
+            # frames can fit the device limit.
+            if (
+                np.any(decoded <= 0)
+                or np.any(decoded > min(_MAX_FRAME_BYTES, maximum))
+                or np.any(encoded <= 0)
+                or np.any(encoded > maximum)
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "GPU-delta frames require positive lengths, <=4 MiB "
+                    f"output and both lengths <= device limit {maximum}"
+                )
+            if np.any(inputs < 0) or np.any(inputs > input_bytes - encoded):
+                raise ValueError("Encoded frame outside input allocation")
+            if np.any(outputs < 0) or np.any(outputs > _INT64_MAX - decoded):
+                raise ValueError("Output arithmetic exceeds signed metadata")
+            if np.any(outputs[1:] < outputs[:-1] + decoded[:-1]):
+                raise ValueError("Overlapping or unordered decoded frames")
+            if np.any((inputs + input_base) % self.alignments.input):
+                raise ValueError("Misaligned encoded frame")
+            remainder = outputs % self.alignments.output
+            first = int(remainder[0])
+            if np.any(remainder != first) or remainders[slot] not in (None, first):
+                raise ValueError("Misaligned decoded frame")
+            remainders[slot] = first
+            bounds[slot] = max(bounds[slot], int(outputs[-1] + decoded[-1]))
+            if count > _INT64_MAX // maximum:
+                raise ValueError("Decoded geometry sum exceeds signed metadata")
+            geometry.append((count, int(decoded.max()), int(decoded.sum())))
+        return geometry, bounds, remainders
+
+    @profiling.annotate("gpu_delta.prepare.decoder_metadata")
+    def prepare_batches(
+        self,
+        table: np.ndarray,
+        counts: Sequence[int],
+        host_input: torch.Tensor,
+        stream: torch.cuda.Stream,
+    ) -> PreparedDecodePlan:
+        """Prepare numeric metadata and small workspace without decoded output.
+
+        Rows contain relative input offsets, encoded sizes, decoded sizes and
+        relative output offsets. The admitted host arena must stay immutable
+        until the DE stream drains. Only input/size rows are uploaded now;
+        ``bind_outputs`` fills output pointers under the serving pause.
+        """
+        from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.memory import device_empty
+
+        if (
+            host_input.device.type != "cpu"
+            or host_input.dtype != torch.uint8
+            or not host_input.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("nvCOMP input must be a contiguous host arena byte view")
+        if stream.device != self.device:
+            raise ValueError("Decoder stream/device mismatch")
+        input_base = host_input.data_ptr()
+        geometry, bounds, remainders = self._frame_geometry(
+            table, counts, input_base, host_input.numel()
+        )
+        with torch.cuda.device(self.device), torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            workspace = self._allocate_workspace(geometry)
+            host = torch.empty(
+                table.shape, dtype=torch.int64, device="cpu", pin_memory=True
+            )
+            host_rows = host.numpy()
+            np.add(table[0], input_base, out=host_rows[0])
+            host_rows[1:3] = table[1:3]
+            metadata = device_empty(host.shape, dtype=torch.int64, device=self.device)
+            if metadata.numel():
+                metadata[:3].copy_(host[:3], non_blocking=True)
+        return PreparedDecodePlan(
+            self,
+            counts,
+            host_input,
+            workspace,
+            host,
+            metadata,
+            stream,
+            table[3].copy(),
+            bounds,
+            remainders,
+        )
+
+
+class PreparedDecodePlan:
+    """Publication metadata and output leases, bound only while paused."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        decoder,
+        counts,
+        host_input,
+        workspace,
+        host_metadata,
+        metadata,
+        stream,
+        output_offsets,
+        output_bounds,
+        output_remainders,
+    ):
+        self.decoder, self.stream = decoder, stream
+        self.workspace = workspace
+        self.host_metadata, self.metadata = host_metadata, metadata
+        self.output_bounds, self.output_remainders = output_bounds, output_remainders
+        # Every batch retains this same list. Binding fills it only after all
+        # output checks pass; dropping the plan alone cannot free in-flight slots.
+        self.decoded_slots = []
+        self.batches = []
+        temporary = workspace.temporary
+        offset = 0
+        for index, count in enumerate(counts):
+            slot = index % 2
+            rows = metadata[:, offset : offset + count]
+            host_rows = host_metadata[:, offset : offset + count]
+            statuses = workspace.statuses[slot, :count]
+            actual_sizes = workspace.actual_sizes[slot, :count]
+            expected_sizes = rows[2]
+            arguments = (
+                rows[0].data_ptr(),
+                rows[1].data_ptr(),
+                expected_sizes.data_ptr(),
+                actual_sizes.data_ptr(),
+                count,
+                temporary.data_ptr(),
+                temporary.numel(),
+                rows[3].data_ptr(),
+                decoder._options,
+                statuses.data_ptr(),
+                stream.cuda_stream,
+            )
+            self.batches.append(
+                PreparedDecode(
+                    decoder,
+                    host_input,
+                    self.decoded_slots,
+                    workspace,
+                    host_rows,
+                    rows,
+                    stream,
+                    statuses,
+                    actual_sizes,
+                    expected_sizes,
+                    arguments,
+                    output_offsets[offset : offset + count],
+                    host_rows[3].numpy(),
+                )
+            )
+            offset += count
+        self.record_stream(stream)
+
+    def record_stream(self, stream):
+        """Register every consumer before it can enqueue storage readers."""
+        from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.memory import record_device_stream
+
+        if stream.device != self.decoder.device:
+            raise ValueError("Decoder consumer stream/device mismatch")
+        for tensor in (
+            self.metadata,

+    workspace: DecodeWorkspace

+    metadata: torch.Tensor
+    stream: torch.cuda.Stream

+    output_offsets: np.ndarray
+    output_pointers: np.ndarray

+        This object and all storage must outlive the submitted work. There is no

+        allocation finalizers also fence their recorded consumers before freeing.
+        """

+"""Prepare small derived consumer values without modifying live model state.
+
+Weight and block-scale permutations belong to byte bindings. These updates only
+handle NVFP4's complete scalar calibration values, never decoded XOR masks.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from itertools import product
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PreparedCopy:
+    destination: torch.Tensor
+    source: torch.Tensor
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class DerivedUpdate:
+    """An update whose inputs can include several independently changed scales.
+
+    ``overrides`` contains complete tensors keyed by ``id(original_source)``.
+    The caller assembles any partial canonical updates before preparation and
+    applies the returned copies only after successful DE/apply completion.
+    """
+
+    sources: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]
+    destinations: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]
+    compute: Callable[[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]], tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]]
+    checks: Callable | None = None
+
+    def prepare(self, overrides: Mapping[int, torch.Tensor]):
+        result, checks = self._prepare(overrides)
+        _validate_checks(checks)
+        return result
+
+    def _prepare(self, overrides):
+        # The batch preparer collects device predicates across layers. Public
+        # prepare() still validates before returning any prepared copies.
+        values = tuple(overrides.get(id(source), source) for source in self.sources)
+        for original, value in zip(self.sources, values):
+            _same_geometry(original, value, "source")
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            outputs = tuple(self.compute(values))
+            if len(outputs) != len(self.destinations):
+                raise ValueError("GPU delta derived output count changed")
+            result, snapshots = [], {}
+            for destination, value in zip(self.destinations, outputs):
+                _same_geometry(destination, value, "destination")
+                # Retain complete target values independently of live buffers;
+                # later source copies must not alter a prepared update.
+                if id(value) not in snapshots:
+                    snapshots[id(value)] = value.detach().clone()
+                result.append(PreparedCopy(destination, snapshots[id(value)]))
+            checks = self.checks(outputs) if self.checks is not None else ()
+        return tuple(result), checks
+
+
+def _validate_checks(checks):
+    if not checks:
+        return
+    # One small transfer/synchronization for the whole prepared update. Keep
+    # individual results so failures retain their original useful diagnostics.
+    passed = torch.stack([predicate for predicate, _ in checks]).cpu().tolist()
+    for ok, (_, message) in zip(passed, checks):
+        if not ok:
+            raise ValueError(message)
+
+
+def _same_geometry(original, value, role):
+    if (
+        not isinstance(value, torch.Tensor)
+        or original.shape != value.shape
+        or original.dtype != value.dtype
+        or original.device != value.device
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(f"GPU delta derived {role} geometry changed")
+
+
+def _storage_key(tensor):
+    return tensor.device, tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+
+
+def _element_offsets(tensor):
+    return [
+        tensor.storage_offset()
+        + sum(i * stride for i, stride in zip(index, tensor.stride()))
+        for index in product(*(range(size) for size in tensor.shape))
+    ]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class _SourcePlan:
+    source: torch.Tensor
+    targets: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class _UpdatePlan:
+    update: DerivedUpdate
+    sources: tuple[_SourcePlan, ...]
+
+
+def plan_updates(updates, targets):
+    """Validate and cache scalar patch geometry once at admission."""
+    by_storage = {}
+    for target in targets:
+        by_storage.setdefault(_storage_key(target), []).append(target)
+    plans = []
+    for update in updates:
+        sources = []
+        for original in update.sources:
+            patches = by_storage.get(_storage_key(original), ())
+            if not patches:
+                continue
+            if not original.is_contiguous():
+                raise ValueError("GPU delta derived source must be contiguous")
+            start, stop = (
+                original.storage_offset(),
+                original.storage_offset() + original.numel(),
+            )
+            written = set()
+            for target in patches:
+                if target.dtype != original.dtype:
+                    raise ValueError("GPU delta scalar view dtype mismatch")
+                offsets = set(_element_offsets(target))
+                if any(offset < start or offset >= stop for offset in offsets):
+                    raise ValueError("GPU delta scalar view is outside its source")
+                if len(offsets) != target.numel() or offsets & written:
+                    raise ValueError("GPU delta scalar updates overlap")
+                written.update(offsets)
+            sources.append(_SourcePlan(original, tuple(patches)))
+        plans.append(_UpdatePlan(update, tuple(sources)))
+    return tuple(plans)
+
+
+def prepare_updates(plans, raw_copies):
+    """Patch cached scalar views, then validate device predicates once per update."""
+    incoming = {
+        id(target): value
+        for targets, values in raw_copies.values()
+        for target, value in zip(targets, values)
+    }
+    prepared, checks = [], []
+    for plan in plans:
+        overrides = {}
+        for source_plan in plan.sources:
+            changed = [
+                target for target in source_plan.targets if id(target) in incoming
+            ]
+            if not changed:
+                continue
+            original = source_plan.source
+            complete = original.detach().clone()
+            for target in changed:
+                value = incoming[id(target)]
+                _same_geometry(target, value, "raw source")
+                offset = target.storage_offset() - original.storage_offset()
+                complete.as_strided(target.shape, target.stride(), offset).copy_(value)
+            overrides[id(original)] = complete
+        if overrides:
+            copies, predicates = plan.update._prepare(overrides)
+            prepared.extend(copies)
+            checks.extend(predicates)
+    _validate_checks(checks)
+    return tuple(prepared)
+

+"""FlashInfer expert layouts expressed as views of live consumer bytes.
+
+The apply kernel knows only affine byte coordinates. These admission-time
+helpers factor the inference backend's permutations into those coordinates.
+They never transform a delta, requantize a weight, or allocate a weight image.
+A segment selects a rectangle of one canonical projection; its destinations
+have the same flattened byte order, and may cover several independent images.
+Padding is deliberately outside every destination.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from enum import Enum
+
+import torch
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class FlashInferLayout:
+    format: str
+    backend: str
+    gated: bool
+    quant_mode: str = ""
+    up_first: bool = False
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class DestinationSegment:
+    # Coordinates are canonical ELEMENTS, not bytes. Only the returned views
+    # use byte coordinates, so BF16 source selections retain their element size.
+    slices: tuple[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]]
+    destinations: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]
+
+
+def _backend(backend):
+    backend = backend.value if isinstance(backend, Enum) else backend
+    return {
+        "flashinfer_trtllm": "trtllm",
+        "flashinfer_trtllm_routed": "trtllm",
+        "flashinfer_mxfp4": "trtllm",
+        "flashinfer_cutedsl": "cutedsl",
+        "flashinfer_megamoe": "megamoe",
+    }.get(backend, backend)
+
+
+def identify_layout(layer, backend):
+    """Identify an existing inference path; do not select or construct one."""
+    backend = _backend(backend)
+    if backend not in {"trtllm", "cutedsl", "megamoe"}:
+        raise ValueError(f"unsupported FlashInfer expert backend: {backend}")
+    method = layer.quant_method
+    if method.runner is not None and _backend(method.runner.runner_backend) != backend:
+        raise ValueError("FlashInfer selection does not match the live expert runner")
+    name = type(method).__name__
+    gated = bool(layer.moe_runner_config.is_gated)
+    if name == "UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod":
+        if backend != "trtllm" or not method.use_flashinfer_trtllm_moe:
+            raise ValueError("no native FlashInfer BF16 expert path for this backend")
+        return FlashInferLayout(
+            "bf16", backend, gated, up_first=method.load_up_proj_weight_first
+        )
+    if name == "ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod":
+        if not method.quant_config.is_checkpoint_nvfp4_serialized:
+            raise ValueError("GPU delta does not admit on-load NVFP4 quantization")
+        mode = "w4a4"
+        if backend == "cutedsl":
+            if not method._is_cutedsl_v2_standard:
+                raise ValueError("GPU delta requires the standard CuTe DSL layout")
+            if layer._cutedsl_wrapper is None:
+                raise ValueError("CuTe DSL warmup must initialize its wrapper")
+            mode = layer._cutedsl_wrapper.quant_mode
+            if mode not in {"w4a4", "w4a16"}:
+                raise ValueError(f"unsupported CuTe DSL quant mode: {mode}")
+        return FlashInferLayout(
+            "nvfp4", backend, gated, mode, up_first=backend == "cutedsl"
+        )
+    if name == "Mxfp4FlashinferTrtllmMoEMethod":
+        if backend != "trtllm" or method._fp8.dequant_fp4_to_fp8:
+            raise ValueError("MXFP4 TRTLLM requires native packed expert weights")
+        return FlashInferLayout("mxfp4", backend, gated, up_first=True)
+    if name == "Mxfp4MoEMethod":
+        if backend != "trtllm" or method._fi_kernel != "trtllm_sm100":
+            raise ValueError("unsupported native MXFP4 FlashInfer expert path")
+        return FlashInferLayout("mxfp4", backend, gated, up_first=True)
+    if name != "Fp8MoEMethod":
+        raise ValueError(f"unsupported FlashInfer expert quantization: {name}")
+    if backend == "cutedsl":
+        raise ValueError("ordinary CuTe DSL MoE has no native FP8/MXFP4 path")
+    if method.dequant_fp4_to_fp8 or method.convert_mxfp8_to_block:
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta does not admit weight requantization")
+    config = method.quant_config
+    if method.use_mxfp8:
+        if not config.is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized:
+            raise ValueError("GPU delta requires serialized MXFP8 weights")
+        return FlashInferLayout("mxfp8", backend, gated)
+    if method.is_fp4_expert:
+        if backend != "megamoe":
+            raise ValueError("native FP4 TRTLLM experts require its MXFP4 method")
+        return FlashInferLayout("mxfp4", backend, gated)
+    if (
+        backend == "trtllm"
+        and config.scale_fmt == "ue8m0"
+        and config.weight_block_size == [128, 128]
+        and config.is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized
+    ):
+        return FlashInferLayout("fp8-block128-ue8m0", backend, gated)
+    raise ValueError("unsupported FlashInfer expert format; native UE8M0 is required")
+
+
+def _bytes(tensor):
+    if tensor.ndim == 0:
+        tensor = tensor.view(1)
+    if tensor.stride(-1) != 1:
+        raise ValueError("FlashInfer image requires contiguous innermost elements")

+                chunk["decoded_offset"],
+                chunk["decoded_offset"] + chunk["decoded_bytes"],
